correctness.rationale: The final claim is hub-rooted flooding on B_{m,k}=K_1 vee (m K_k) with independent Exp(1) edges, m->infinity and EVERY sequence k=k_m>=2. A hub path cannot profit from traversing another petal. Within one K_{k+1}, successive exploration waits are independent Exp(i(k+1-i)/k) after multiplying flood time by k. Exactly the first and last rates equal one; the internal exponential tilt has exact residue product A_k=(k-1)^2, mean mu_k=2kH_{k-2}/(k-1), uniformly bounded centered variance and exponential moment. The gamma-two survival function and exponential tilt yield m P(kR_k>b+x)=e^{-x}[1+(log log m+x+1+delta_k)/log m]+O_x(m^(-1/12)/log m), delta_k=2log(k-1)-mu_k bounded uniformly in k. Independence across m petals produces the Gumbel and marked Poisson limits; the first/last independent rate-one waits have uniform ratio independent of completion time. k=1 is treated separately as a maximum of m Exp(1) edges. The critical computations were rederived for representative k from the source rate formula and the infinite uniform bound follows analytically, not by finite simulation.
residual_risks: No extension to nonhub roots, non-exponential edges or arbitrary petal graphs; the claimed O(log m) and m^-1/12 remainder concerns a fixed x and uniform k.
Finite k computations cannot establish the uniform k->infinity statement; that depends on the bounded tilted variance and exponential Markov estimates.

value.rationale: A changing-petal-size first-passage model is natural: a hub links many dense modules, and neither the number of modules nor the within-module size must stay fixed. A size-uniform second-order extreme-value estimate and marked Poisson process require a nontrivial tilted-concentration mechanism and distinguish otherwise identical fixed-k approximations. The result provides a reusable exact distributional boundary and quantitative error; the earlier finite-size factorization alone does not give the desired arbitrary growth regime.
residual_risks: Conditional on exactly rate-one independent exponential passage times and the fixed hub/petal geometry.
